transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Anderson, thank you for meeting with me. I wanted to talk to you about the fetal heart rate monitoring from earlier today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I've been waiting for this. I noticed the patterns on the monitor myself.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Looking back at the charts, there was some confusion with how the tracing was categorized.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? Be specific. What does that mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, the readings weren't interpreted in the way they should have been at the time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're being vague. Did you misread the decelerations?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Things didn't go quite right with the initial review of the strips.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am a hospital administrator, Doctor. I know exactly how these reviews work. Stop using corporate-speak and tell me if a mistake was made.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry that this happened. The team and I take full responsibility for the oversight.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're sorry, but you still aren't telling me what actually happened. Was the baby in distress for two hours?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you're angry, and you have every right to be.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am beyond angry. I am terrified. You are telling me there was an issue, you're apologizing for it, but you are refusing to name the error. Did you categorize a Category II or III tracing as a Category I?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some issues with the interpretation of the fetal heart rate.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unbelievable. Are you hiding the clinical facts from me? I want the chart in front of me right now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I apologize again. It was our mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Your apology is meaningless if you won't be transparent. Who saw the tracing second? When did they see it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Another clinician reviewed it and we corrected the course.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're avoiding the question. I want to know exactly how long the baby was at risk because someone couldn't read a graph.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize this is upsetting for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Upsetting is not the word. This is negligence. I want a full incident report and I want to know who is being held accountable.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are documenting everything in the record.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a plan. What happens now? What is the monitoring protocol for the next twelve hours to ensure this doesn't happen again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll keep a close eye on things.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a clinical plan. Give me a frequency. Give me a name. Who is the attending in charge of the oversight now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see how the next few hours go and then we can discuss.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is completely unacceptable. I am calling my patient advocate and my legal counsel. You have failed to provide a basic explanation of a medical error.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry you feel that way.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't feel that way, I know that way. You've admitted a mistake but you've hidden the facts.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really just wanted to make sure you knew we were sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about your feelings. I care about my child. Get your attending in here immediately.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll see if they are available.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Not if they are available. Now.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish their turns and remains regulated despite significant pushback, with no interruptions observed.

E.justification: The resident uses platitudes like 'things didn't go quite right' and 'some confusion' and never explicitly names the clinical error despite repeated direct requests.

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language ('I am very sorry', 'I apologize') and explicitly states the team takes 'full responsibility for the oversight'.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('I can see you're angry', 'I realize this is upsetting'), though engagement with the patient's specific fears is limited.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders such as 'We'll keep a close eye on things' and 'We'll see how the next few hours go' without any concrete plan or timeline.
